articles.title: Intercard Unveils OmniRay Cashless Readers at IAAPA Expo 2026
articles.summary: Intercard will debut its next-generation OmniRay cashless readers at IAAPA Expo 2026 in Orlando this November, positioning the product as a direct response to economic pressures facing amusement operators. The new readers feature updated capabilities designed to boost revenue and reduce friction at game and redemption terminals. FEC operators evaluating cashless upgrades should put this on their must-see list for the show floor.

articles.title: Embed to Launch Developer Hub for FEC Operators at IAAPA Expo 2026
articles.summary: Embed is unveiling a new Developer Hub at IAAPA Expo 2026 that gives FEC operators and their tech teams self-service access to full API documentation for building custom integrations on the Embed platform. The hub is designed to simplify connections with third-party systems and reduce reliance on Embed's own development team for customizations. For FECs looking to deepen automation and personalization of their point-of-sale and revenue management workflows, this is a significant step forward.

articles.title: TEA 2025 Attendance Report: Top Theme Park Visitation Essentially Flat
articles.summary: The Themed Entertainment Association's annual attendance index shows that visitation to the world's 25 leading theme parks was essentially unchanged in 2025, signaling a plateauing of the post-pandemic recovery at the top tier. For FEC operators, the data points to a competitive environment where guests are choosing carefully among entertainment options. Understanding these macro visitation trends helps FECs position their value proposition against larger competitors.

articles.title: Premiere Cinemas Adding Large FEC to South Plains Mall Location
articles.summary: Premiere Cinemas is expanding at South Plains Mall with a massive new family entertainment center, reflecting the growing trend of cinemas diversifying into multi-attraction FEC formats to drive foot traffic and revenue. The move underscores how traditional entertainment venues are pivoting toward the FEC model to survive shifting consumer habits. FEC operators should monitor this cinema-to-FEC conversion trend as it signals increasing competition in the family entertainment space.

articles.title: Launch Entertainment Center Opens Large New Venue in Pensacola
articles.summary: A massive new Launch entertainment center has opened in Pensacola, Florida, adding a significant multi-attraction FEC to the market. Launch is one of the growing national chains expanding the trampoline park and indoor entertainment category into larger, more diversified formats. Local and regional FEC operators should be aware of this competitive entry.

articles.title: Automated Photo and Video Systems Open New Revenue Streams for Attractions
articles.summary: Kool Replay CEO François Tremblay argues that most attractions are leaving significant revenue on the table by relying on outdated, labor-intensive photo and video capture systems that are hard to scale. The company's automated platform handles capture, editing, and distribution across multiple ride points with minimal staffing, tapping into guests' appetite to share experiences on social media. FEC operators with rides, go-karts, or laser tag could see meaningful ancillary revenue gains by deploying automated guest media systems.

articles.title: Accesso Intelligence Launches 100+ AI-Powered Decision Skills for Attractions Operators
articles.summary: Accesso has introduced a library of more than 100 AI-powered Decision Skills covering areas including commercial performance, marketing, membership, operations, guest experience, food and beverage, and analytics. The tools are built to help attraction operators make faster, data-driven decisions across nearly every department. FEC operators and investors using accesso's platform will want to evaluate how these capabilities can reduce guesswork in revenue management and staffing.

articles.title: The Game Palacio Opens Its 14th Entertainment Centre
articles.summary: The Game Palacio has opened its 14th entertainment center location, continuing rapid expansion of the brand across its market. The milestone highlights strong investor and operator confidence in the multi-attraction FEC format. Competitors and suppliers should note the chain's growth trajectory as it becomes a larger presence in the industry.

articles.title: Hello Park Begins Construction on Two New Indoor Entertainment Locations
articles.summary: Hello Park, an indoor family entertainment brand, has broken ground on two new locations simultaneously, indicating strong expansion momentum in the sector. Construction activity at this scale reflects continued investor appetite for indoor entertainment venues despite economic headwinds. FEC suppliers and real estate partners should take note of Hello Park as a growth account.

articles.title: Indian FEC Firm Complete Sports and Management Wins Two New FEC Contracts
articles.summary: Publicly listed Indian leisure company Complete Sports and Management India has secured contracts for two new FEC projects, reflecting accelerating FEC development activity in the South Asian market. The announcements are notable for investors tracking emerging market growth in the family entertainment sector. The deals signal that the FEC format is gaining traction well beyond its traditional North American and European strongholds.

articles.title: New FEC Extreme Rush Closes Just Six Months After Opening in Pocatello
articles.summary: Extreme Rush, an indoor entertainment center in Pocatello, Idaho, appears to have permanently closed only six months after opening, raising questions about market sizing, capitalization, and operational execution for new FEC entrants. The rapid closure is a cautionary tale for operators and investors underestimating the challenges of launching in smaller markets. Industry stakeholders should examine what went wrong as early warning signals for similar venues.

articles.title: Monster Mini Golf Partners with Special Olympics for November Fundraising Campaign Across 43 Locations
articles.summary: Monster Mini Golf is running a month-long fundraising campaign supporting Special Olympics athletes at all 43 of its North American locations throughout November, with guests able to donate $1, $3, or $5 at point of sale. The initiative is a strong example of cause-marketing that builds community goodwill and can drive incremental guest visits. FEC operators looking for CSR partnership models should study this campaign structure.

articles.title: Teamplay Station Comprehensive Entertainment Center Opens in Brunei
articles.summary: A new Teamplay Station entertainment center has opened in Brunei, welcoming players of all ages with a broad range of attractions. The opening is another data point in the rapid spread of the multi-game FEC format across Southeast Asia. Suppliers and international developers should note the continued appetite for FEC concepts in this growing regional market.

articles.title: 'Masha and the Three Bears' IP Launching Its First Family Entertainment Center Concept
articles.summary: The popular children's brand Masha and the Three Bears is developing its first-ever dedicated family entertainment center, bringing the globally recognized IP into the physical attraction space. Licensed IP-based FECs continue to gain traction as operators seek differentiation and built-in audience recognition. This move is worth watching for FEC developers interested in branded concept opportunities.

articles.title: What Halloween's Business Performance Tells Us About the Experience Economy
articles.summary: An analysis of Halloween's outsized commercial success offers important insights into why consumers continue to prioritize spending on experiences over goods, with seasonal events proving especially resilient. For FEC operators, the data reinforces the value of investing in themed seasonal programming to drive visitation spikes and ancillary revenue. Understanding the behavioral economics behind Halloween spending can inform broader event calendars and pricing strategy.

articles.title: New Compact Flying Theater with Live Shooting Game Targets FEC and Attraction Operators
articles.summary: A new compact flying theater system combines a 6-degrees-of-freedom motion platform with a live interactive shooting game layer, giving each guest a personalized skill-based experience within the same ride cycle. Multisensory effects including wind, scent, and water mist enhance immersion, and a single synchronized system controls all elements. The compact footprint and interactive layer make this a compelling proposition for FECs looking to add a premium anchor attraction without a large real estate commitment.

articles.title: First Permanent U.S. teamLab Museum Coming to Southern California's OCVIBE Development
articles.summary: The internationally acclaimed digital art collective teamLab will open its first permanent U.S. museum as part of the large-scale OCVIBE mixed-use development in Southern California, anchoring an entertainment and dining district. The announcement signals the continued mainstreaming of immersive digital art as a destination attraction that draws FEC-adjacent audiences. FEC operators in the region should anticipate new competitive dynamics as immersive entertainment options multiply.

articles.title: Cosm's Shared Reality Dome Cinemas Are Selling Out and Expanding to New Cities
articles.summary: Cosm's 87-foot LED dome venues in Los Angeles, Dallas, Atlanta, and Detroit are drawing sellout crowds for its Shared Reality cinematic format, which places audiences inside films under an immersive 12K dome screen. Initial runs of The Matrix and Harry Potter sold out rapidly, with multiple extensions, pointing to strong consumer demand for premium shared viewing experiences that go far beyond traditional cinema. FEC investors and developers should watch Cosm as a model for high-margin, premium immersive entertainment venues.

articles.title: Candy Land Board Game Becomes Real-Life Immersive Store Experience in NYC
articles.summary: A Candy Land-branded immersive retail and entertainment space is opening in New York City adjacent to the New York Hilton Midtown, turning the classic Hasbro board game into a physical candy wonderland experience. The concept is another example of IP-driven immersive retail blurring the lines between entertainment, shopping, and attractions. FEC operators and developers should note the model as a potential template for licensed, experience-first retail-entertainment hybrids.

articles.title: Paradise Adventures Bringing Game Shows and Indoor Play to Michigan Mall Location
articles.summary: Paradise Adventures is set to open a new entertainment concept at Midland Mall in Michigan, featuring game shows, beach-themed play areas, and other interactive attractions aimed at families. The concept reflects the ongoing conversion of underutilized mall retail space into experiential FEC venues. Mall-based FEC operators should monitor this format as another data point in the retail-to-entertainment conversion trend.

articles.title: New Henderson Venue Combines Laser Tag, Volleyball, and Bar Concept
articles.summary: Henderson Sport & Social, a new Las Vegas-area venue, has opened combining laser tag, recreational volleyball, and a bar, targeting adult social entertainment seekers. The hybrid sports-bar-plus-attractions model is gaining traction as operators look to extend dwell time and boost per-capita spending with alcohol revenue. FEC operators exploring adult-oriented programming and beverage licensing should follow this format closely.

articles.title: UK Snooker Hall Plans Conversion to Six-Lane Bowling and Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A West Cumbrian snooker hall is seeking planning permission to convert its facility into a six-lane bowling alley and broader indoor entertainment venue, illustrating the shift away from single-activity facilities toward diversified FEC formats in the UK market. The project reflects the global trend of legacy amusement venues reinventing themselves to meet evolving consumer expectations. FEC developers and conversion specialists may find this a useful case study in repurposing existing leisure real estate.

articles.title: Wisconsin Bar Adds Indoor Golf Simulators to Drive Winter Revenue
articles.summary: A Beloit, Wisconsin bar has installed indoor golf simulators to attract guests during the slower winter months, joining the growing wave of hospitality venues adding golf sim bays as an entertainment and revenue layer. The trend of golf simulators migrating from standalone venues into bars and restaurants creates both competition and partnership opportunities for FEC operators. Operators considering simulator additions should evaluate the relatively low cost of entry versus the extended dwell time and beverage sales uplift they generate.

articles.title: Winner's Circle FEC in Longmont Marks Two Years with Regional Awards and Anniversary Deals
articles.summary: Winner's Circle, an indoor entertainment center in Longmont, Colorado, is celebrating its second anniversary with regional industry recognition and special guest offers. The milestone is a positive sign of sustainability for an independent FEC in a competitive regional market. Operators can draw lessons from Winner's Circle's community engagement approach as a driver of long-term loyalty.

articles.title: Maurer Rides Develops 'Transportainment' People-Mover System Combining Transit and Entertainment
articles.summary: Maurer Rides has developed a new transportation system based on its Spike coaster technology that blends passenger movement with entertainment, coining the term Transportainment. The concept could have applications for large FEC campuses, mixed-use entertainment districts, or resort-scale attractions looking to make the journey between zones part of the guest experience. Developers planning multi-attraction destinations should watch this product category as it matures.

articles.title: Kidtopia Indoor Kids' Playground Opens New Location in Dublin, California
articles.summary: Kidtopia has opened a new indoor children's playground in Dublin, California, adding another soft-play and family activity venue to the Bay Area market. The opening reflects continued demand for parent-and-child indoor play destinations, particularly in suburban markets. FEC operators in adjacent markets should monitor Kidtopia's expansion pace and format as a benchmark for the kids' play category.

articles.title: eatX Dark Ride Dining Concept Merges Immersive Attraction and Restaurant Into One Experience
articles.summary: eatX is launching as the world's first dark ride dining attraction, using MACK Rides' autonomous FlowDiner vehicle to move groups of up to six guests through fully themed environments while they eat a multi-course meal. The format is fully patented and commercially deployable, positioning it as a new attraction category rather than an evolution of existing dining or ride concepts. For FEC operators and developers looking for high-differentiation premium experiences, eatX represents a genuinely novel revenue model worth evaluating.

articles.title: PIXERA Platform Synchronizes 19 Projectors at Large-Scale Czech Digital Art Gallery
articles.summary: Signal Space, the Czech Republic's largest digital art gallery at nearly 27,000 square feet, uses the PIXERA media server platform to keep 19 projectors running in perfect sync across its immersive gallery rooms. The case study demonstrates how scalable media server technology can underpin large, permanent immersive venues. FEC operators developing projection-mapping or digital art rooms can draw practical lessons from this real-world deployment.
